title: Operator Handoff QuickPanel — compact GPU-pool control and health brief
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, actionable panel for the Redwood Console that enables on-call operators and platform engineers to quickly assess GPU pool health, surface high-signal telemetry, and perform common handoff actions (temporary burst, scale override, annotate incident, and create follow-up runbook tasks). This QuickPanel lives as a slide-over from pool lists and a sticky widget in the pool detail header. Primary goals: reduce mean time-to-resolution during capacity incidents, make burst configuration auditable, and offer a low-friction handoff flow between operators and SREs.
comments: 2025-01-14 - Maya Chen: Kickoff sketching session with ENG and PM. Agreed to prioritize concise telemetry + 3 primary actions (Burst, Throttle, Annotate).
2025-01-22 - Liam O'Connor: Mid-fidelity mockups uploaded. Added microcopy option for 'temporary burst' to clarify duration semantics. Asked ENG about backend support for ad-hoc bursts (ENG-19872).
2025-01-28 - Priya Rao (PM): Suggested adding a lightweight cost estimate before applying burst (approx tokens/min and projected daily spend). Marked as required for customer-facing flows.
2025-02-03 - Alex Park (Infra Eng): Feasibility note — we can support burst durations up to 6 hours; need an API change for annotated audit entries (ENG-19935).
2025-02-10 - Design review: Feedback to make battery of health signals reorderable and to expose 'playbook link' per pool. Asked to prototype keyboard accessibility for quick actions.
decisions: Keep QuickPanel content density low: single-column stack with 5 canonical signals (SLO breach, queue depth, avg latency p95, GPU utilization, burstable headroom).
Primary actions limited to 3: Temporary Burst, Scale Throttle, Create Annotated Incident. More advanced controls moved to full pool detail page.
Bursts are timeboxed with explicit default durations (15m, 1h, 4h) and require a short free-text reason for auditability.
Cost preview included inline: show estimated cost delta and a confidence band (low/medium/high) computed by Optimize heuristics.
RBAC: QuickPanel actions gated by role; viewers see telemetry only. Implemented via existing RBAC layer (no new permission model).
tradeoffs: Compact vs. comprehensive: Chose higher information scent at the cost of hiding deeper historical traces — users can jump to full pool page for detailed traces.
Action friction vs. speed: Requiring a short reason increases latency to apply bursts but is necessary for audit and postmortem traceability.
Cost estimate accuracy: We surface a rough estimate to reduce surprise, but it may be inaccurate for highly variable workloads. Marked as advisory only.
user_test_summary: Conducted 5 moderated sessions with on-call SREs (internal). Key findings: 1) SREs value immediate cost delta and default burst durations, 2) desire for quick 'snooze alerts' action, 3) keyboard shortcuts for burst/annotate reduce time-to-action in simulated incidents. Minor accessibility issues found with focus order in slide-over — fixed in v1.1 prototype.
next_steps: Resolve ENG API gaps: ENG-19935 to add annotated audit endpoint (blocking).
Ship engineering spike to implement cost preview hook (ENG-19872).
Finalize copy and microcopy for all actions; hand to Content for review.
Schedule 1-week pilot with two customers on Dedicated Beta and collect telemetry on action frequency and user feedback.
Implement keyboard interaction tests and update accessibility checklist before engineering handoff.
